description: PondToPlot helps small farmers in El Salvador's Bajo Lempa and Bay of Jiquilisco who run a fish/shrimp pond next to a crop field. They log pond water quality (oxygen, pH, ammonia, temperature, salinity) and the tool combines it with NASA data (GPM IMERG, SMAP, NDVI, ECOSTRESS, NASA POWER) to recommend when to irrigate with nutrient-rich pond water, wait for rain, or exchange water, and to compare crop-rotation strategies.
summary: PondToPlot is a decision-support web tool for small producers in El Salvador's Bajo Lempa and Bay of Jiquilisco who farm a fish or shrimp pond next to a crop field. Pond water is usually drained and wasted, even though it carries nitrogen the field needs; traditional aquaculture loses about 79% of feed nitrogen and 83% of feed phosphorus to the environment. Farmers log simple test-kit readings (dissolved oxygen, pH, ammonia, temperature, salinity). PondToPlot combines them with NASA Earth observations (GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture, MODIS NDVI, and NASA POWER daily rain, soil wetness and temperature), a crop water-stress input designed for ECOSTRESS, plus a 3-day rain forecast. Five ordered, explainable rules then recommend whether to irrigate with nutrient-rich pond water, wait for rain, or exchange/aerate the pond, and always show why. It also suggests seasonal crop rotations: nutrient-hungry crops in the dry season using pond water, and legumes in the rainy season. The tool saves water, recycles nutrients, protects soil from salt, and supports rather than replaces farmer judgment.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
PondToPlot answers one daily question for producers who farm a pond and a field side by side: what should I do with my pond water today? It returns one of three actions, each with a plain-language reason: (1) irrigate the field with pond water, because it brings nitrogen; (2) wait, because rain is coming or the soil is already wet; or (3) exchange or aerate the pond, because oxygen, pH, ammonia or temperature are risky. Brackish ponds are never used for irrigation, to avoid salting the soil. A rotation panel suggests nutrient-hungry crops (maize, vegetables) in the dry season when fresh pond water is available, and legumes (beans) in the rainy season to restore soil nitrogen and break pest cycles. A logbook stores every reading and exports to CSV, turning the paper logbook habit into data.

HOW IT WORKS
The farmer enters test-kit readings. The tool pulls NASA POWER daily data for the farm (PRECTOTCORR rain, GWETTOP topsoil wetness, T2M_MAX temperature) and a 3-day rain forecast, and shows NASA GIBS map layers for GPM IMERG precipitation, SMAP L4 soil moisture and MODIS NDVI over the Bajo Lempa and Bay of Jiquilisco. Five ordered rules (salinity, water health, rain/soil moisture, nutrient value plus crop need, no action) decide the recommendation, and the matching rule is highlighted so the logic is transparent.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Saves water by reusing pond water and skipping irrigation before rain; recycles nutrients that traditional aquaculture loses (about 79% of feed nitrogen and 83% of feed phosphorus, Kabir et al., Water 2026); protects soil from salinization; and gives small producers access to NASA data without GIS skills. It supports, never replaces, farmer judgment and local experts.

TOOLS
Single-page web app in HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Leaflet for maps, NASA GIBS WMTS tiles, the NASA POWER API, and the Open-Meteo forecast API, hosted on GitHub Pages.

CREATIVITY AND CONSIDERATIONS
It treats the pond as a water source with fertilizer included, linking aquaculture and crop rotation. It starts with explainable rules instead of a black-box model, because AI models that reach over 90% accuracy in pilots often drop to about 75% on commercial farms (Kabir et al., 2026). Thresholds are general reference values to be validated with aquaculture experts; demo pond readings are synthetic and labeled as such. Next: field pilot with a Bajo Lempa cooperative, full rotation-strategy comparison with farmer priorities, and a Phase 2 model trained on farmers' logbooks.

Landsat / HLS NDVI (planned field-scale NDVI; MODIS NDVI used in prototype)
